title: Pairs Below a Sum Limit
statement:
You get an integer array nums and an integer target. Count the index pairs (i, j) with i < j whose sum nums[i] + nums[j] is strictly less than target.

Pairs are of positions, so equal values at different positions form separate pairs.

examples.why: The pairs summing to 2, 3 and 0 count. 3 + 1 = 4 is not strictly less than 4.
-6 pairs with all four others (sums −4, −9, −6 and −5), and -3 + 0 = −3 also counts. The condition does not care which index comes first, so sorting the values does not change the count.

hints: The answer only depends on which values are paired, not on their positions. What does that let you do to the array first?
After sorting, fix the smallest remaining value at the left. If it plus the largest remaining value is below target, what about it plus everything in between?
Two pointers lo and hi: if nums[lo] + nums[hi] < target, all hi − lo partners of lo count, so add them and move lo right. Otherwise hi is too big for everyone left, so move hi left.

explain.intuition:
The condition i < j only stops you from counting a pair twice; the sum does not depend on order. So you can sort the values and count pairs of positions in the sorted array instead.

In sorted order, put lo at the start and hi at the end. If nums[lo] + nums[hi] < target, then nums[lo] plus anything between them is also below target, because those values are no bigger than nums[hi]. That settles hi − lo pairs in one step, and lo moves on. If the sum is too big, nums[hi] is too big even for the smallest partner left, so it can be dropped. Each step retires one pointer position, so after the sort the scan is O(n).
steps: Sort a copy of nums ascending. Set lo = 0, hi = n − 1, count = 0.
While lo < hi: if nums[lo] + nums[hi] < target, add hi − lo and move lo right.
pitfalls: Using ≤ instead of <. In the first example, 3 + 1 = 4 must not count.
Adding 1 instead of hi − lo when the sum fits, which counts one pair per step instead of all of them.
Sorting with JavaScript's default sort(), which compares as strings and breaks on negatives and multi-digit numbers.

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: Two nested loops over i < j, counting sums below target.

solutions.title: Sort and binary search
solutions.idea: For each position i in sorted order, binary search how many later values are below target − nums[i].

solutions.title: Sort and two pointers
solutions.idea: If the smallest and largest fit, every value in between fits with the smallest too: count them all and advance lo. Otherwise drop the largest.
